historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mushtaque Ali Khan, a Mughal Emperor (1627-1658 AD) who ruled the Deccan region of India. The name Mushtaque carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mushtaque Ali Khan was the eldest son of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. He founded the Adil Shahi dynasty in the Deccan region after the fall of the Bijapur Sultanate. He is best known for his military conquests and for building the magnificent Bidar Fort.

historical_references.reference: Mirza Rukn-ud-Din Firuz Shah 'Mushtaque', the last independent ruler of the Bahmani Sultanate (1538-1565 AD).
historical_references.context: Mushtaque was the second son of Sultan Salim Shah Suri. He came to power after the death of his father and had to face rebellions from within his own court. He tried to maintain peace and order, but was ultimately defeated by the Deccan Sultanates and the Mughal Empire. He is best remembered for his patronage of literature and art.
